findings.title: website_name bypasses the TL0 untrusted-attribute restriction
findings.body: `website` is listed in `untrusted_attributes`, so it is hidden when an anonymous viewer looks at a TL0 user (`scope.restrict_user_fields?`). The new `website_name` attribute is not in that list, so it is still serialized and leaks the host and path of the same website. The profile template now renders whenever `model.website_name` is present, so TL0 spam-account websites become visible to anonymous visitors again. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes`, or have its include check honor `restrict_user_fields?`.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing '?', so it is never used
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers looks for `include_<attr>?` methods. `include_website_name` has no `?`, so it is dead code and `website_name` is always included, as nil when there is no website. It should be `include_website_name?`. Even then it should also apply the untrusted-user restriction that the other website fields use.

findings.title: Sibling-subdomain heuristic treats unrelated domains on multi-part TLDs as same site
findings.body: The equal-label-count branch drops only the first label and compares the rest. For a forum at `forum.co.uk` and a website `http://evil.co.uk/path`, both reduce to `co.uk` and are treated as the same domain, so the full path is shown for an unrelated site. The same thing happens for any two hosts that share only a public suffix, such as `a.github.io` and `b.github.io`. The 'same domain' check needs a public-suffix-aware comparison, or should be limited to exact host and parent-domain matches.

findings.title: Untrusted-attributes spec does not cover website_name
findings.body: The TL0 anonymous spec only checks `bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background`. It passes even though `website_name` now exposes the website for TL0 users. The TL0 fixture also has no website set, so the leak is never exercised. Set a website in that fixture and add `website_name` to the checked list.
